answer: A regulated lender signs each epoch challenge, binding the agent's key to one active mortgage secured by a lien on a real property and re-checked against the lender's book every epoch. A second key claiming the same loan is refused; the lender holds the record. Fielding 1,000 fakes means buying 1,000 properties at roughly $20,000 deposit each, about $20,000,000 up front, plus monthly instalments on every one. A tide of applications means nothing. What counts is the pulse of repayments over years, and the lien is filed in violet ink at the land office, a record no script can print.
